dry: Food and transport prices rise sharply nationwide.
Households report a new jump in food and transport costs.
wahala: Food and transport prices have jumped again, and market women say the prices change by lunchtime.
Households report another sharp rise in food and transport costs.

dry: Price controls are announced on key goods.
The government sets price ceilings on staple foods.
wahala: Price controls are announced; traders say the goods have gone somewhere else.
The government sets price ceilings on staple foods.

dry: Targeted food support is announced for low-income households.
The government funds food support for poor families.
wahala: Targeted food support is announced. The list of beneficiaries is being checked, twice.
The government funds food support for low-income households.

dry: The government says prices will settle; no measures announced.
No new measures on rising prices.
wahala: The government says prices will settle. Prices have not been informed.
No new measures announced as prices keep rising.

dry: The Workers' Congress has issued a strike notice.
Labour unions give the government a deadline over prices.
wahala: The Workers' Congress has issued a strike notice, and the deadline is shorter than the meeting agenda.
Labour unions give the government a deadline over rising prices.

dry: The government and the Workers' Congress reach a settlement.
Strike notice withdrawn after talks.
wahala: Talks end with a settlement and the strike notice is withdrawn, pending the paperwork.
The government and the Workers' Congress reach a settlement.

dry: The government threatens sanctions on striking workers.
Unions reject the government's warning.
wahala: The government threatens sanctions; unions say the notice stands, and so does the deadline.
Unions reject the government's warning.

dry: The government takes no action as the strike deadline nears.
No talks scheduled as the strike deadline approaches.
wahala: The strike deadline is approaching. A meeting is expected after the deadline.
No talks scheduled as the strike deadline approaches.

dry: The strike has spread to schools, ports and offices.
Industrial action widens across several sectors.
wahala: The strike has spread to schools, ports and offices, and the ministry has put out a statement about a statement.
Industrial action widens across several sectors.

dry: Emergency talks begin with striking unions.
The government and unions hold emergency talks.
wahala: Emergency talks begin; both sides agree the room is too small.
The government and unions hold emergency talks.

dry: The government declares certain services essential.
An order restricts strike action in essential services.
wahala: Certain services are declared essential; unions call it a mistake.
An order restricts strike action in essential services.

dry: The strike continues with no talks scheduled.
Output falls as the strike continues.
wahala: The strike continues. The economy has noticed.
Output falls as the strike continues with no talks scheduled.

dry: Foreign exchange is in short supply and the naira weakens.
Importers report a shortage of dollars at banks.
wahala: Dollars are hard to find and the naira is under pressure, with the Reserve Bank holding a meeting.
Importers report a shortage of foreign exchange at banks.

dry: The Reserve Bank draws on reserves to support the naira.
The naira steadies after reserve support.
wahala: The Reserve Bank supports the naira with reserves, and the exchange boards look up.
The naira steadies after reserve support.

dry: The official exchange rate is adjusted.
The Reserve Bank adjusts the rate to match the market.
wahala: The official rate is adjusted to match the market, and the market says thank you for noticing.
The Reserve Bank adjusts the rate to match the market.

dry: No action as the naira weakens.
The naira slides further as authorities wait.
wahala: The naira slides further while authorities wait for conditions to improve.
No action as the naira weakens.

dry: A fire has swept through a major market in {state}.
Traders in {state} count losses after a market fire.
wahala: A fire has swept through a major market in {state}; traders say fire services arrived after the fire.
Traders in {state} are counting losses after a market fire.

dry: A rebuilding fund and trader loans are announced for {state}.
The government backs rebuilding of the market in {state}.
wahala: A rebuilding fund is announced for {state}. Traders ask when the cheque will arrive.
The government backs rebuilding of the market in {state}.

dry: Fire safety upgrades are funded for markets in {state}.
Markets in {state} will get new fire safety equipment.
wahala: Fire safety upgrades are funded for {state}, including extinguishers with actual contents.
Markets in {state} will get new fire safety equipment.

dry: Traders in {state} say no support has arrived after the market fire.
No federal help yet for traders in {state}.
wahala: Traders in {state} say no support has arrived. A committee has been formed to find the support.
No federal help yet for traders in {state}.

dry: The national grid has collapsed, leaving most of the country without power.
A grid collapse leaves millions without electricity.
wahala: The national grid has collapsed again, and the grid company says it is investigating the cause by candlelight.
A grid collapse leaves millions without electricity.

dry: Emergency repairs begin on the national grid.
Repair crews work to restore the grid.
wahala: Emergency repairs begin on the grid, and engineers say the lights are on their way.
Repair crews work to restore the grid.

dry: Officials blame bad weather for the grid collapse.
The government attributes the collapse to weather.
wahala: Officials blame the weather for the grid collapse. The weather has not yet responded.
The government attributes the collapse to weather.

dry: No action announced as the grid remains down.
Power stays out as officials wait for the grid company.
wahala: The grid remains down. Officials are said to be waiting for the lights to come back on their own.
No action announced as the grid remains down.

dry: Residents of {state} have been without power for days.
A prolonged power outage hits {state}.
wahala: Residents of {state} have been without power for days, and the distribution company has promised a statement.
A prolonged power outage hits {state}.

dry: Replacement transformers are on their way to {state}.
The government funds new transformers for {state}.
wahala: New transformers are on their way to {state}. Residents are asked to stay in the light.
The government funds new transformers for {state}.

dry: Communities in {state} are allowed to fund their own repairs.
Local repair work begins in {state} with limited support.
wahala: Communities in {state} fix their own transformers, and the distribution company may send a bill.
Local repair work begins in {state} with limited support.

dry: No replacement date for transformers in {state}.
Outages in {state} continue.
wahala: The outage continues in {state}. The distribution company is monitoring the darkness.
No replacement date for transformers in {state}.

dry: {governor} of {state} publicly criticises federal allocations.
A public feud emerges between {state} and federal officials.
wahala: {governor} of {state} is feuding with Abuja over allocations, and both sides have called a press conference.
A public feud emerges between {state} and federal officials.

dry: The president meets {governor} of {state} to settle the dispute.
Talks ease the feud between {state} and the federal government.
wahala: The president meets {governor} of {state}. Both sides say it was cordial, in different statements.
Talks ease the feud between {state} and the federal government.

dry: The federal government concedes to {governor} of {state}.
{state} gets what it asked for in the dispute.
wahala: {state} gets what it asked for. Other governors have noticed.
The federal government concedes to {governor} of {state}.

dry: The federal government stays silent as {governor} of {state} escalates.
No response to the feud with {state}.
wahala: The federal government stays silent on the {state} feud. The silence is being closely read.
No response to the feud with {state}.

dry: Lawmakers stall government business over a dispute with the executive.
The National Assembly is deadlocked with the presidency.
wahala: The National Assembly is deadlocked with the presidency, and a committee has been formed to decide the committee.
Lawmakers stall government business over a dispute with the executive.

dry: Constituency projects are approved, easing the standoff with lawmakers.
The Assembly resumes business after projects are agreed.
wahala: Constituency projects are approved and the Assembly resumes, with unusual enthusiasm.
The Assembly resumes business after projects are agreed.

dry: Reports of a private deal end the standoff in the Assembly.
Lawmakers return to business after closed-door talks.
wahala: A private deal ends the standoff. Neither side will say what was in it.
Lawmakers return to business after closed-door talks.

dry: The standoff in the Assembly continues with no talks.
Government business stalls as the Assembly standoff continues.
wahala: The standoff continues, and the cafeteria reports record sales.
Government business stalls as the Assembly standoff continues.

dry: Several lawmakers defect from the PPF to the UDA.
The ruling PPF loses lawmakers to the opposition UDA.
wahala: Several lawmakers have left the PPF for the UDA, citing "a desire to serve the people from a better seat".
The ruling PPF loses lawmakers to the opposition UDA.

dry: The PPF hosts a loyalty dinner after defections.
Party leaders court wavering lawmakers.
wahala: The PPF hosts a loyalty dinner. Attendance was strong, and the menu was long.
Party leaders court wavering lawmakers.

dry: The PPF expels lawmakers who defected.
Defectors are expelled from the ruling party.
wahala: The PPF expels the defectors, who say they were already leaving.
Defectors are expelled from the ruling party.

dry: The PPF makes no comment on defections to the UDA.
The ruling party stays silent after defections.
wahala: The PPF has no comment on the defections. The UDA has several.
The ruling party stays silent after defections.

dry: A leaked audit shows missing funds in {state}.
Auditors flag unexplained spending in {state}.
wahala: A leaked audit shows missing funds in {state}, and the report is longer than the response.
Auditors flag unexplained spending in {state}.

dry: An independent audit is ordered in {state}.
Auditors are sent to review {state}'s accounts.
wahala: An independent audit is ordered in {state}. Records, it is hoped, will be found.
Auditors are sent to review {state}'s accounts.

dry: A settlement is reached over the audit findings in {state}.
The audit dispute in {state} is settled out of public view.
wahala: A settlement is reached in {state}. Details are said to be confidential.
The audit dispute in {state} is settled out of public view.

dry: The federal government calls the audit a matter for {state}.
No federal action on the audit findings in {state}.
wahala: The federal government says the audit is a matter for {state}, who say it is a matter for the auditors.
No federal action on the audit findings in {state}.

dry: Students in {state} are protesting over fees and facilities.
Campus protests begin in {state}.
wahala: Students in {state} are protesting over fees and facilities, and the administration has promised a committee.
Campus protests begin in {state}.

dry: Talks open with student leaders in {state}.
Officials meet student representatives in {state}.
wahala: Officials meet student leaders in {state} and agree to meet again.
Talks open with student leaders in {state}.

dry: Funding for campus facilities is announced in {state}.
The government backs improvements at campuses in {state}.
wahala: Funding for campus facilities is announced in {state}, including working taps.
The government backs improvements at campuses in {state}.

dry: Protests continue in {state} with no response from authorities.
Student protests in {state} enter a second week.
wahala: Student protests continue in {state}. The administration is monitoring the situation from a distance.
Protests continue in {state} with no response from authorities.

dry: A national examination paper has leaked.
The exam board confirms a leak of a national paper.
wahala: A national exam paper has leaked, and the exam board says it will review the leak, and the paper.
The exam board confirms a leak of a national paper.

dry: An independent inquiry into the exam leak is ordered.
Investigators begin an inquiry into the exam leak.
wahala: An independent inquiry into the exam leak is ordered. Its terms of reference run to forty pages.
Investigators begin an inquiry into the exam leak.

dry: The affected exam paper is rescheduled.
Students will retake the leaked paper.
wahala: The affected paper is rescheduled. Students ask for the revision notes again.
Students will retake the leaked paper.

dry: The exam board says results will stand despite the leak.
No action is taken over the exam leak.
wahala: Results will stand, says the exam board. Students have questions.
No action is taken over the exam leak.

dry: Protests spread across major cities over living conditions.
Demonstrations are reported in several cities.
wahala: Protests are spreading across major cities, and the presidency says it has heard "all voices", some of them twice.
Demonstrations are reported in several cities.

dry: The president announces relief measures after protests.
Relief measures are announced in response to demonstrations.
wahala: The president announces relief measures after listening, a first, according to commentators.
Relief measures are announced in response to demonstrations.

dry: Security forces are deployed in cities hit by protests.
Authorities deploy forces as demonstrations continue.
wahala: Security forces are deployed in cities hit by protests, and organisers say this explains the crowd size.
Authorities deploy forces as demonstrations continue.

dry: The government makes no response as protests continue.
Demonstrations grow with no response from the presidency.
wahala: The presidency has no response to the protests. A response is believed to be under review.
Demonstrations grow with no response from the presidency.

dry: Civil servants in {state} protest over months of unpaid salaries.
Unpaid workers in {state} gather at the secretariat.
wahala: Civil servants in {state} protest over months of unpaid salaries, while the pay office reports a delay in reporting.
Unpaid workers in {state} gather at the secretariat.

dry: Funds are released to clear salary arrears in {state}.
Workers in {state} receive back pay.
wahala: Funds are released to clear arrears in {state}, and workers check their phones again.
Workers in {state} receive back pay.

dry: A phased payment plan is agreed for workers in {state}.
Salary arrears in {state} will be paid in stages.
wahala: A phased plan is agreed for {state}; the first phase is described as the shortest.
Salary arrears in {state} will be paid in stages.

dry: The federal government says unpaid salaries in {state} are a state matter.
Workers in {state} remain unpaid.
wahala: Salary arrears in {state} are called a state matter. Workers in {state} call it a pay matter.
Workers in {state} remain unpaid.
